concept.title: Ideal-string tension belongs to each body-specific FBD
concept.inferential_jump: For one taut massless ideal string, with any redirection treated as frictionless and massless, the tension magnitude can be represented by one T throughout that same string; each body still receives its own tension force along the local string direction.
entry_assumptions: Can assign forces to the body they act on.
Can apply Newton II to a chosen body.

teaching_path.action: State the idealization before using one tension symbol: taut inextensible massless string, with any pulley/redirection frictionless and massless for this bounded model.
teaching_path.why_valid: Uniform tension is a consequence of the ideal model and must not be silently transferred to a nonideal rope or pulley.
teaching_path.output: ideal single string model declared -> one tension magnitude T is admissible throughout that string

teaching_path.action: For each attached body, draw the string's pull along the local string direction away from the body.
teaching_path.why_valid: Tension is a force exerted by the string on that body and belongs on that body's FBD.
teaching_path.output: body A FBD contains string-on-A force of magnitude T; body B FBD contains string-on-B force of magnitude T

teaching_path.action: Use the same symbol T for those magnitudes only while the declared ideal assumptions hold.
teaching_path.why_valid: A massless string segment cannot sustain a nonzero net force in this idealized model, and a frictionless massless redirection does not create a tension-magnitude jump.
teaching_path.output: T_A = T_B = T under the declared ideal-string/redirection conditions

teaching_path.action: Check whether the problem introduces rope mass, elasticity, pulley friction, or rotational inertia; if it does, stop using equal tension unless a different model justifies it.
teaching_path.why_valid: Those changes alter the force transmission assumptions that supported one common T.
teaching_path.output: nonideal feature present -> equal-tension relation not licensed by this capability

teaching_path.action: Determine the tension magnitude from a chosen body's signed Newton-II equation; do not replace T by mg or by an applied force merely because those forces appear in the same setup.
teaching_path.why_valid: Uniform tension says the ideal string transmits one magnitude throughout itself; it does not say that magnitude equals some different force. For a hanging body, T=mg only in the special zero-acceleration case.
teaching_path.output: for +y upward on a hanging mass: T - mg = ma_y; therefore a_y=0 -> T=mg, a_y>0 -> T>mg, and a_y<0 -> T<mg.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Tension forces at the two ends of a string cancel because they are equal and opposite.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Do the two end tensions act on the same chosen body?
misconceptions.repair: No. Put the tension force acting on each body in that body's own FBD. Equal magnitudes across the ideal string do not make them a cancelling pair on one body.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Every rope over every pulley has the same tension on both sides.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: What model assumptions justify using one symbol T throughout the rope?
misconceptions.repair: State the ideal massless string and frictionless/massless redirection assumptions first. Without them, equal tension is not automatic.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The tension in a string holding a hanging mass is always equal to the mass's weight.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A hanging mass accelerates upward. Can T still equal mg while Newton II gives a nonzero upward net force?
misconceptions.repair: Write the signed body equation. With upward positive, T-mg=ma, so upward acceleration requires T>mg; equality belongs only to zero vertical acceleration.

relation_checks: Each tension force is assigned to the body it acts on.
Breaking an ideal assumption requires the equal-tension claim to be re-evaluated.

exit_task.prompt: Two bodies are attached to the same taut ideal string, redirected only by a frictionless massless fixed pulley. State the tension relation and explain where the two tension forces appear.

answer.summary: Under the declared ideal model, both string segments have the same tension magnitude T. Each body has its own string-on-body tension force on its own FBD; the forces are not cancelled across separate body diagrams.
reasoning: The ideal assumptions license one common tension magnitude throughout the same string.
Each tension force acts on a different body and points along that body's local string segment.
Equal magnitude does not mean the forces cancel in an individual-body equation.
answer.check: If the pulley is explicitly frictional or the rope has significant mass, this capability must refuse to assume equal tension.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The exit states the model-conditional symbolic equality of tension magnitudes and assigns the forces to their bodies; no numerical tension is computed.
